title: Entry criteria, recursion control, performance, and maintainability
objectives: Write Start-element entry conditions that keep a record-triggered Flow from running on every save.
Use ‘only when the record is updated to meet the condition requirements’ to reduce recursion and repeat work.
Order multiple Flows on one object with Flow Trigger Explorer and trigger order values (1–2000).
Explain maintainability: one job per Flow, descriptions, and why after-save Update Records on the triggering record is a recursion risk.
diagnostic_question: An after-save Flow updates the triggering Opportunity and fires itself until it hits a limit. What entry-criteria setting and which Update placement would you change first?
definition: Entry criteria are the Start-element conditions that decide whether a record-triggered Flow even begins. Recursion control is keeping that Flow from re-entering because it updated the same record. Performance is reducing unnecessary interviews (entry conditions, before-save when it fits, no extra Gets). Maintainability is ordering and owning Flows so the next admin can change one job without reading ten canvases. ([Triggered Flows](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger.htm); [Planning Your Switch to Flow Builder](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_migrate_to_flow_best_practices.htm))
why_it_matters: A Flow with no entry conditions runs on every edit. An after-save Update of the triggering record can call the Flow again. Interviewers listen for ‘updated to meet the condition’, Flow Trigger Explorer, and before-save versus after-save—not a vague ‘we optimized it’.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a thermostat, not a fan that never stops. Entry criteria are the temperature threshold: only run when the room crosses 72°F. ‘Updated to meet the condition’ is hysteresis: do not cycle again just because the AC is still on. Recursion is the AC cooling so hard it retriggers itself. Flow Trigger Explorer is the panel that sequences two thermostats on the same floor (order 1–2000). The wiring diagram is metadata; the room temperature is data.
deeper_explanation: Help: add conditions on the Start element so the Flow runs only when necessary. Planning Your Switch: entry conditions decrease performance impact and prevent unnecessary runs. You can require a field to have a value, or enable Run When Conditions Met so the Flow runs when a record is created or edited and a field is changed to a specified value. That setting prevents repeat operations. ([Bulkify example / entry conditions](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.automate_flow_build_example_bulkified_processing.htm); [Planning Your Switch](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_migrate_to_flow_best_practices.htm))

Triggered Flows: before-save Fast Field Updates change the triggering record before save and are described as about 10 times faster than a record-change process. After-save is for related records. Updating the triggering record again in after-save can start another save and another interview—the usual recursion story. ([Triggered Flows](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger.htm))

Flow Trigger Explorer shows record-triggered Flows for an object and trigger type. You can assign a trigger order value from 1 to 2000 so before-save or after-save Flows on the same object run in a predictable sequence. ([Triggered Flows](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger.htm))

Planning Your Switch: migration is not one Flow per old process; structure by performance, maintenance, and change management. Multiple Flows per object are manageable if you order them. Identify redundant automation. ([Planning Your Switch](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_migrate_to_flow_best_practices.htm))
Bulk-safe DML (AUTO-007) is still the other half of performance. Entry criteria that never fire are faster than a perfectly bulkified Flow that runs on every chatter-edit of Description.

mental_model.analogy: A thermostat with hysteresis: threshold = entry criteria, ‘updated to meet’ = do not retrip while already in band, runaway AC = recursion, two thermostats on one floor = trigger order 1–2000.
useful_mapping: entry conditions → temperature threshold on the Start element
Run when conditions met / updated to meet → hysteresis so the same true condition does not retrip every save
after-save Update of $Record → AC that changes the thermostat setting and starts another cycle
before-save Assignment → adjust the same save without a second trip
Flow Trigger Explorer → panel listing every thermostat on that object
trigger order 1–2000 → which thermostat runs first
Flow metadata → wiring diagram; record field values → room temperature
where_it_breaks: Some platform updates (for example certain approval field updates) can fire Flows more than once despite entry criteria—Needs verification against current known issues.
Trigger order does not replace order of execution across validation rules, Apex, and assignment rules.
ISCLONE() in entry criteria has had debug limitations; prefer a Decision if Debug fails.
The analogy does not encode CPU time numbers.

telugu_glossary.telugu: Start element conditions on a record-triggered Flow.
The Flow runs again because it updated the same record.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Entry criteria on Start decide if the interview begins. Use ‘updated to meet the condition’ so a still-true Stage does not retrip. Prefer before-save for same-record fields. After-save Update of the triggering record can recurse. Order multiple Flows 1–2000 in Flow Trigger Explorer.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I treat every-edit Flows as a performance bug. I write Start conditions like Stage equals Closed Won and, when the requirement is the transition, I enable the updated-to-meet setting from Planning Your Switch. I put same-record stamps in before-save. I use Explorer when two teams own after-save Flows on Opportunity. I still bulkify DML (AUTO-007). I do not claim trigger order replaces the full save order of execution.

terminology.plain: Start-element conditions that must be true for the record-triggered Flow to run.
terminology.precise: Condition requirements on the triggering record (and optionally the updated-to-meet / Run When Conditions Met behavior).
terminology.example: Stage equals Closed Won on Opportunity after-save.
terminology.non_example: A Decision in the middle of the canvas after the Flow already started.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Decision element: runs only after entry criteria already passed.
terminology.boundary: Formula entry criteria exist; some formulas (historically ISCLONE) have had Debug limits.

terminology.plain: Run when the record changes into the criteria, not on every later save that still matches.
terminology.precise: Planning Your Switch: Run When Conditions Met / field IS CHANGED to a value prevents repeat operations.
terminology.example: Closed Won Flow does not run again when Amount is edited while Stage stays Closed Won.
terminology.non_example: Conditions Are Met with no updated-to-meet, so every Closed Won edit starts the Flow.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: ISCHANGED in a formula: related idea; UI checkbox is the interview-friendly name.
terminology.boundary: Create-only triggers do not need the same hysteresis story.

terminology.plain: The Flow causes another save that starts the same (or another) Flow again.
terminology.precise: Common pattern: after-save Update Records on the triggering record. Entry criteria and before-save reduce it. Do not invent that the platform never re-enters.
terminology.example: After-save sets LAB_Stamp__c on the Opportunity, which is another update.
terminology.non_example: A Loop over a collection inside one interview (that is iteration, not save recursion).
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Scheduled path: a later interview, not the same-save recursion loop.
terminology.boundary: Apex static recursion guards are a different tool.

terminology.plain: The tool that lists record-triggered Flows for an object and trigger type.
terminology.precise: Help: view, filter, reorder, and navigate before-save, after-save, and asynchronous paths for an object.
terminology.example: Open Opportunity after-save and see three Flows plus their order.
terminology.non_example: The Automation app Flows list with no object filter.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Debug: one interview, not the object’s full trigger set.

terminology.plain: A number from 1 to 2000 that sequences same-object before-save or after-save Flows.
terminology.precise: Define the Run Order of Record-Triggered Flows: assign a trigger order value so Flows run in a predictable sequence.
terminology.example: Validation-prep Flow at 1000, Task-create Flow at 1100.
terminology.non_example: Order of execution position versus validation rules (different framework).
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Scheduled path timing: clock time, not trigger order.
terminology.boundary: Needs verification of ties/default when two Flows share a number.

terminology.plain: before-save record-triggered Flow optimized for the triggering record.
terminology.precise: Help: about 10 times faster than a record-change process; limited elements; no related Create.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: after-save Update Records on $Record: slower and recursion-prone.

terminology.plain: Whether the next admin can find, order, and change the automation without a scavenger hunt.
terminology.precise: Planning Your Switch: who owns the process, likelihood of change, not one-to-one migration, order with Trigger Order.
terminology.example: One after-save Flow named LAB_Opp_ClosedWon_Tasks with a description and order 1100.
terminology.non_example: Twelve unnamed after-save Flows that all start with no entry conditions.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Subflow reuse: a maintainability tactic, not a trigger-order substitute.

terminology.plain: Avoiding interviews and database work the business does not need.
terminology.precise: Entry conditions first, before-save when it fits, bulk-safe DML (AUTO-007), fewer redundant Flows.
terminology.example: Closed Won entry so Description edits do not Get team members.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Async path: higher limits later, not a substitute for entry criteria.
terminology.boundary: Do not quote unofficial CPU milliseconds.

mechanics.before: No conditions; runs on every create/update of the object
mechanics.after: Conditions match the business event (for example Stage equals Closed Won)
mechanics.observe: Debug of a non-matching edit does not start the interview
mechanics.failure: Empty Start conditions ‘so we can Decision later’

mechanics.after: Run only when the record is updated to meet the conditions, if the event is the transition
mechanics.observe: Editing Amount on an already Closed Won Opportunity does not create duplicate Tasks
mechanics.failure: Leaving updated-to-meet off when the requirement is the Stage change

mechanics.after: before-save Assignment for stamps; after-save for related Create/Update/Delete
mechanics.observe: No second save for the stamp field
mechanics.failure: After-save Update Records on the triggering record for a simple stamp

mechanics.trigger: More than one Flow on the object
mechanics.after: Trigger order 1–2000 in Flow Trigger Explorer; description states owner and job
mechanics.observe: Explorer list matches the intended sequence

when_to_use: When a record-triggered Flow needs Start entry criteria so it does not run on every save.
When you must stop repeat interviews with ‘updated to meet the condition’ / Run When Conditions Met.
When after-save Update Records on the triggering record risks recursion and before-save is the better stamp.
When several Flows on one object need Flow Trigger Explorer and trigger order 1–2000 for maintainability.
When performance work starts with fewer interviews, not only fewer Get Records.
when_not_to_use: Do not use entry criteria as a substitute for bulk-safe Create/Update/Delete (AUTO-007).
Do not claim trigger order replaces the full Salesforce order of execution.
Do not turn off entry criteria in production to ‘debug faster’ and leave them off.
Do not put related-record Create in before-save in the name of performance.
Do not invent a numeric recursion cap; verify current platform behavior.
configuration_or_code_location: Flow Start: object, trigger, condition requirements, updated-to-meet / Run When Conditions Met.
Optimize the Flow for Fast Field Updates vs Actions and Related Records.
Flow Trigger Explorer: object + trigger type + trigger order 1–2000.
Flow properties: label, API name, description, owner in the description.

decisions.rejected: No entry conditions, Decision after a Get of all team members

configuration_or_code: before-save: Stage equals Closed Won; Assignment sets LAB_Closed_Won_Date__c.
after-save: Stage equals Closed Won AND updated to meet; Get/Assign/Create Tasks (AUTO-007).

verification: Debug a Stage change to Closed Won runs both intended interviews.
Debug an Amount-only edit on Closed Won does not create more Tasks.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable sandbox; LAB_ Opportunity fields only.
starting_state_checks: You can create record-triggered Flows and open Flow Trigger Explorer.
A custom date or checkbox field exists for a stamp.
steps: Create an after-save Flow with no entry conditions that Updates a stamp and note how often it runs in Debug.
Add Stage equals Closed Won and updated-to-meet; Debug an Amount-only edit.
Move the stamp to a before-save Flow; keep related work after-save.
Set trigger order values in Flow Trigger Explorer and record them.
guided_completion: If Amount edits still create work, updated-to-meet is off or the Flow Updates $Record again.
If before-save tries to Create Tasks, that is the wrong optimize setting.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Add a second after-save Flow on the same object and assign a later trigger order; prove Explorer lists both.
evidence: Notes: Debug runs with and without updated-to-meet.
stop_recovery_cleanup: Clear LAB_ stamp fields if needed.
hands_on_lab.limitations: This lab does not prove maximum CPU time or approval-process double-fire known issues.

decision_table.signal: Need to stamp a field on the same record that just changed.
decision_table.choose: before-save Fast Field Updates with Start entry criteria.
decision_table.not: after-save Update Records on the triggering record for that stamp.
decision_table.why: Before-save is the faster same-record path and avoids an extra save that can recurse.

decision_table.signal: Closed Won should create Tasks only when Stage becomes Closed Won, not on later Amount edits.
decision_table.choose: Start conditions plus run only when the record is updated to meet them.
decision_table.not: No entry criteria and a Decision after Get Records of team members.
decision_table.why: Planning Your Switch: entry conditions and Run When Conditions Met prevent repeat operations.

decision_table.signal: Two teams own after-save Flows on Opportunity and testers see unpredictable Task timing.
decision_table.choose: Flow Trigger Explorer and explicit trigger order values between 1 and 2000.
decision_table.not: Merge both into one unnamed Flow without discussion, or ignore order.
decision_table.why: Help: assign trigger order so same-object Flows run in a predictable sequence.

decision_table.signal: Every Description edit on Account starts a Flow that Gets Contacts.
decision_table.choose: Tighten Start entry criteria so the interview does not begin.
decision_table.not: Only micro-optimize the Get after the Flow already started.
decision_table.why: The cheapest interview is the one that never starts.

decision_table.signal: You are migrating several Process Builder processes on one object.
decision_table.choose: Redesign into fewer Flows with entry criteria and order; not one Flow per old diamond.
decision_table.not: Literal one-to-one migration with no Start conditions.
decision_table.why: Planning Your Switch: migration is not one-to-one; structure for performance and maintenance.

limitations: Does not replace AUTO-007 bulk DML rules.
Trigger order is not the full save order of execution.
Some platform features can still double-fire interviews; verify known issues.
Formula entry criteria can be harder to Debug.
security_notes: Entry criteria are not a security control; execution context is AUTO-009.
Do not put confidential filter values in Flow descriptions that all builders can see if that violates policy.
common_mistakes: After-save Update of the triggering record for a simple stamp.
Using a Decision instead of entry criteria so every save still starts.
Ignoring Flow Trigger Explorer when many Flows share an object.
Leaving updated-to-meet off when the event is a transition.

flashcards.back: Repeat interviews when the record still matches but did not newly enter the criteria.

flashcards.front: Common recursion pattern in after-save Flows?
flashcards.back: Update Records on the triggering record, causing another save and another interview.

flashcards.front: Why prefer before-save for a same-record stamp?
flashcards.back: Help: about 10 times faster than a record-change process, and it avoids a second save.

flashcards.front: What is Flow Trigger Explorer for?
flashcards.back: See, filter, reorder, and open record-triggered Flows for an object and trigger type.
1 to 2000 for before-save or after-save Flows on the same object.
Entry criteria can skip the interview. A Decision runs after the Flow already started.

flashcards.front: Planning Your Switch on one-to-one migration?
flashcards.back: Not required. Redesign, remove redundant processes, and order Flows.
A Loop iterates in one interview. Recursion is another save that starts automation again.

flashcards.front: Amount edits create more Closed Won Tasks. Check what?
flashcards.back: Updated-to-meet is off, or the Flow updates the triggering record and retriggers.

flashcards.front: Does trigger order replace order of execution?
flashcards.back: No. It only sequences Flows on that object/trigger. Validation and Apex still have their save-order slots.
Start entry criteria so Get Records never runs on irrelevant edits.
A name that states object, event, and job, plus a description with owner—not ‘Opportunity Flow 2’.

flashcards.front: Can before-save Create related Tasks for performance?
flashcards.back: No. Fast Field Updates cannot Create related records. Use after-save for that DML.

flashcards.front: Are entry criteria metadata or data?
flashcards.back: The conditions are Flow metadata. The Stage value that satisfies them is record data.

interview_questions.question: How do you keep a record-triggered Flow from running too often?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Put real entry criteria on Start. If the event is a transition, enable updated-to-meet / Run When Conditions Met. Do not start the Flow just to Decision after a Get.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cite Planning Your Switch and the Closed Won example. I write the business event as Start conditions. I explain hysteresis so Amount edits do not retrip Closed Won work. I still bulkify DML. I mention Explorer if many Flows share the object.
interview_questions.example: Stage equals Closed Won plus updated-to-meet on the Task Flow.
tradeoffs: Tight criteria vs missing a legitimate edit
weak_answer_warnings: Empty Start and a Decision after Get Records

interview_questions.question: What is recursion in record-triggered Flow, and how do you control it?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The Flow updates the triggering record and starts another save. Prefer before-save for stamps, tight entry criteria, and updated-to-meet. Do not claim Flows never re-enter.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I distinguish a Loop from a new save. I move same-record writes to Fast Field Updates. If after-save must touch $Record, I use a guard field or criteria that the second save does not meet—and I verify current platform recursion behavior instead of quoting a blog cap. I test with two edits in sandbox.
interview_questions.example: After-save set LAB_Stamp__c caused a second interview; stamp moved to before-save.

interview_questions.question: Closed Won creates five Tasks, then every Amount edit creates five more. Diagnose.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The after-save Flow is still matching Closed Won on every update. Turn on updated-to-meet and check for an Update of the Opportunity that retriggers.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I Debug an Amount-only change and watch whether Start is entered. I inspect entry criteria and the updated-to-meet checkbox. I look for Update Records on $Record. I do not blame the user for ‘saving twice’ until those are checked. I add Explorer if a second Flow also creates Tasks.
interview_questions.example: Conditions Are Met without updated-to-meet on Stage equals Closed Won.
follow_ups: What if they change Stage away and back to Closed Won?
weak_answer_warnings: Adding a Decision after Get without fixing Start

interview_questions.question: Two after-save Flows on Account seem to overwrite each other’s field. What tool do you open?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Flow Trigger Explorer for Account after-save. I read both canvases, assign trigger order 1–2000, and decide if they should be one maintainable Flow.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not guess order. Explorer lists the set. I check whether both lack entry criteria. I talk to both owners—Planning Your Switch asks who is responsible. I do not hide the conflict by adding more Decisions. Full order of execution still includes Apex I cannot see in Explorer.
interview_questions.example: Flow A order 1000 sets Status; Flow B order 1200 sets Status again.
tradeoffs: Two ordered Flows vs one Flow
Entry criteria vs letting both run
follow_ups: What if a managed package owns one Flow?
weak_answer_warnings: Saying order is random and unfixable

interview_questions.question: How do you design for maintainability on a busy object?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: One job per Flow, clear names, descriptions with owners, Start criteria, Explorer order, and no one-to-one clone of every old process.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use Planning Your Switch questions: performance, who maintains it, chance of change. I split before-save stamps from after-save related work. I refuse twelve ‘Opportunity Flow’ names. Versioning and tests are AUTO-013, but I mention them as the release side of maintainability.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Account_TypeChange_OwnerAlert at order 1500 with a description naming the sales-ops owner.
tradeoffs: Fewer larger Flows vs more small ordered Flows
follow_ups: When is a subflow worth it?
How do you document trigger order?
weak_answer_warnings: One giant Flow with no Start conditions

interview_questions.question: Debug says the Flow did not run. It is active. Walk the Start checks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Compare the Debug record to entry criteria, create versus update, and updated-to-meet. If you used a formula like ISCLONE, Debug may fail even when runtime works—Needs verification; try a Decision instead.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I read Start first, not the middle of the canvas. I pick a record that should match and one that should not. I check the trigger type. I look at Explorer to be sure I am debugging the version I think I am (AUTO-013). I do not deactivate everything on the object as step one.
interview_questions.example: Debug used an already Closed Won record while updated-to-meet was on.
follow_ups: Can you Debug as another user?

interview_questions.question: Where does performance work start: entry criteria or bulkification?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Both. Entry criteria avoid interviews. Bulk-safe Get/Create/Update/Delete avoid limit errors when interviews do run. Neither replaces the other.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I tell a story: a perfectly bulkified Flow that runs on every Description edit still wastes Gets. A tightly filtered Flow that Create Records inside a Loop still dies on Data Loader. I cite both Help articles. Async paths are a later escape hatch, not the first answer.
interview_questions.example: Closed Won entry plus collection Create after the Loop.
tradeoffs: Tight filters vs missing edge edits
follow_ups: When do you use an asynchronous path?
weak_answer_warnings: Only talking about Loops, or only talking about filters

interview_questions.question: An interviewer asks you to ‘just put everything in one after-save Flow with Decisions so it is easier.’ Respond.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A single Flow with no entry criteria still starts on every save. I will use Decisions inside a Flow that already should run, but I will not skip Start conditions or before-save stamps for convenience.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I acknowledge one canvas can be easier to find. Then I apply Planning Your Switch: performance, ownership, change rate. I may keep related Closed Won work together after a tight Start. I will not mix unrelated Account automations just to have one Flow. I will still set trigger order if another Flow remains. Maintainability is findable jobs, not the fewest XML files at any cost.
interview_questions.example: Closed Won Tasks and Closed Won date stamp: two Starts (before/after), not one unfiltered after-save.
tradeoffs: One Flow vs two typed Flows
follow_ups: When do you use a subflow?
